title: Lanterns Blows Up TV with Manhunter's Death
seoTitle: Lanterns Blows Up TV with Manhunter's Death
subtitle: The series' shocking turn leaves DC fans stunned
excerpt: HBO just released episode 5 of Lanterns, where Zoe Macon, played by Poorna Jagannathan, dies at the hands of John Stewart and Hal Jordan.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
HBO's Lanterns series reached its most dramatic point when, in episode five, the character Zoe Macon, revealed to be the Manhunter, was killed by John Stewart. The episode also features an intense confrontation between Hal Jordan, played by Kyle Chandler, and John, which culminates with John taking the ring and the lantern.

Episode Five Delivers an Explosion of Action and Drama

Geeta Vasant Patel, the episode's director, described the scene as a test of all the emotions built up in the series' first weeks. She emphasized the importance of balancing action with character moments, explaining that the battle scene between Hal and John was designed to reveal the pains and motivations of both characters.

Zoe Macon, the Manhunter, Makes Her Final Appearance

Poorna Jagannathan's character, Zoe Macon, was revealed as the Manhunter in a previous episode. In the fifth episode, the character dies at the hands of John Stewart, marking the end of her arc in the series.

Hal Jordan Faces a Moral Dilemma

During the battle, Hal Jordan does not use his powers but confronts John Stewart as an ordinary man. The confrontation ends with John taking the ring and the lantern, symbolizing a shift in power within the story.

Impact on the Plot and the DC Universe

  • John Stewart takes the ring, altering the balance among the Lanterns.
  • Hal Jordan questions the value of his actions, reflecting on his choices.
  • Zoe's death concludes the Manhunter saga in Rushville.

Fan and Critic Reactions

Viewers noted the plot's intensity, while critics highlight how the series blends elements of crime and superheroes, creating a drama that goes beyond simple power battles.

With information from Los Angeles Times, TheWrap, Variety.
